input.quote: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES.
input.rationale: Section 7(a) does contain a nominally mutual cap and 7(b) has a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, but the clause fails the fallback on carve-outs and on cap basis. The only stated exception is "CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9", and Paragraph 9 is the Independent Contractor clause — so the exception is an inoperative cross-reference and there is no carve-out for confidentiality (§ 8), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement (the § 5(c) non-infringement warranty) or indemnification (the document contains no indemnity clause at all despite the § 7 heading). The fallback requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; none survive here. The basis is also narrower than 12 months' fees: Contractor's cap is limited to fees actually paid for the particular Services under the relevant Statement of Work, which for a short or partly-invoiced SOW can fall below six months' fees. We therefore moved to the preferred position — mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with the standard Excluded Claims sentence uncapped, and confirming Clear Capital's fee payment obligations are not capped damages.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap a mutual 12-months'-fees/USD 1M cap with standard uncapped carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We reset the cap to our standard mutual formulation — the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000 — because the current per-Statement-of-Work "fees paid" basis can fall well below a meaningful amount. We also added the standard carve-out sentence so confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap (the existing exception cross-refers to Paragraph 9, which is the independent contractor clause), and confirmed that fees due are not capped damages.

COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
ops.newText: (a) EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE TO CONTRACTOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (II) USD 1,000,000. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. COMPANY'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE TREATED AS DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.
